title: On-prem K8s Provisioner Integration Runbook
body:
Purpose: This document is a practical runbook for integrating the on-prem provisioner (PXE/IPMI + vSphere) with our Terraform modules and the cluster bootstrap flow. Target audience: SREs / platform eng / solutions eng doing field installs or private customer handoffs. Scope and notes: (short, purposely rough) - Covers: hw inventory -> provisioning -> control-plane bootstrap -> join flows -> post-install telemetry + proactive upgrade plan. - Excludes: deep networking (CNI design) and application manifests. We'll cross-link to the CNI checklist. - Status: working draft, contains commands, TODOs, and open questions. Low ceremony. Assumptions: - Customer has racked gear or reachable vSphere endpoint with datacenter/cluster prepared. - BMC access (IPMI/iLO/iDRAC) with credential rotation plan exists. - Provisioner service (tftp/dhcp/pxe) either on-site or in lab accessible via jumpbox. - Terraform state stored in backend (s3/remote) and teams have write access. High-level flow (one-liner steps): 1) Preflight inventory and hardware tags 2) Configure provisioner (PXE templates, ignitions, image builds) 3) Run Terraform to create provisioning job objects (baremetal/vsphere resources) 4) Bootstrap primary control-plane (kubeadm or k0s) with external etcd or stacked etcd depending on config 5) Join workers, validate telemetry, attach monitoring 6) Post-install hardening and a canary upgrade exercise Preflight checklist (quick): - Verify rack IDs, serials, and NIC MACs for the machine list (CSV). - BMC reachable: ipmitool -I lanplus -H -U -P chassis status - Confirm NTP on BMC and planned nodes. Time skew >120s causes cert issues. - vSphere: check resource pool, datastore, and network port groups exist. - SSH keypair for jumpbox and terraform runner. - KMS/HSM integration required? (Y/N) - if yes, escalate to security. Terraform module notes (practical implementation hints): - Module pattern: use one top-level module per "provisioning target": baremetal_provisioner and vsphere_provisioner. Keep terraform files small and composable. - Example var usage (in module block): module "prov_bm" { source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//provisioner-baremetal" machines_csv = "./inventory/nodes.csv" bmc_creds_id = var.bmc_creds_id pxeboot_template = local.pxe_template_id } - State concerns: lock state per-site (separate backend per-customer/region) to avoid accidental cross-site deletes. - idempotence: modules must be tolerant to partial failures. Use lifecycle { ignore_changes = [metadata[0].annotations] } sparingly for known controller churn. - Outputs to wire to deployment pipeline: control_plane_ips, bootstrap_token, join_cmd (as redacted string). Avoid storing full kubeconfigs in state. - Secrets: avoid plaintext in tfvars. Use remote secret manager (vault/kms) and interpolate with provider data sources where possible. - Retry strategy: some providers (IPMI, vendor APIs) are flaky. Use local-exec with exponential backoff wrapper for critical steps. Provisioner integration quirks (field notes): - NIC ordering: vendor returns inconsistent interface naming; rely on MAC-to-name mapping in ignition, not predictable eth0 names. - PXE caching: some racks have L3 caching devices that cause old tftp files to be served; bump image filenames and TTL when debugging. - vSphere linked clones vs full clones: linked clones faster but can cause snapshot chain issues for long-lived tenant images. Default to full clones for production. - BMC power cycle latencies vary; expect up to 120s in some firmware. Don't tighten timeouts. Bootstrap patterns (recommended): - Control-plane bootstrap should be single-node first (kubeadm init --control-plane-endpoint set to loadbalancer if HA planned). Capture the exact kubeadm config YAML in runbook. - For HA: provision 3 control-plane VMs/nodes, configure API LB, then join with kubeadm join --control-plane. - External etcd: prefer external managed etcd for large fleets. If using stacked etcd, include clear etcd snapshot/restore steps in upgrade playbook. Join flow and post-install validation: - Join worker: capture join command via terraform output join_cmd (short-lived). Example: kubeadm join :6443 --token --discovery-token-ca-cert-hash sha256: - Post-install smoke tests: kubectl get nodes, kubectl get cs, deploy minimal nginx pod with hostNetwork=false to check CNI. - Telemetry bootstrapping: verify node-exporter, kubelet metrics, and logs shipped to central collection. Upgrade plan (proactive and reversible): - Goal: zero-downtime upgrades with clear rollback path. - Canary set: pick 2-3 non-critical workers and run full cluster upgrade there first. Steps: drain -> upgrade kubelet -> restart kubelet -> validate pods -> uncordon. - Control-plane: upgrade control-plane nodes one at a time. Always ensure etcd health after each control-plane upgrade. - Kubelet upgrade order: control-plane first, then workers. If using DaemonSets that depend on exact kubelet ABI, test in canary. - Rolling back: keep pre-upgrade etcd snapshots and cluster-snapshot of manifests. If kubelet version mismatch breaks scheduling, revert kubelet binary and restart. Rollback exercises (runbook drills): - Pre-schedule: run a Canary rollback drill quarterly in staging. - Exercise: simulate failed control-plane upgrade (e.g., broken static pod manifest) and perform etcd restore from latest snapshot. Document exact restore commands here. - Validate restore: ensure kube-apiserver presents same certs/keys and node objects. Clean up orphaned podsand controllers. Common troubleshooting snippets (copyable): - Check etcd cluster health: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints= endpoint health - If node stuck NotReady: journalctl -u kubelet -b --no-pager | tail -n 200 - reset a node for re-provision: wipefs -a /dev/sdX && ipmitool -I lanplus -H -U -P

chassis power reset Observability and post-install hygiene: - Ensure long-term logs are forwarded before any destructive ops. We lost historical capture once when cluster was nuked. - Tag assets in inventory with terraform resource ids for easier support. - Capture network MTU per rack and feed to CNI config (mismatched MTU is a frequent root cause). Open questions / TODOs (short list): - How to best surface join_cmd without leaking tokens to CI logs? (options: ephemeral secret mount in runner, short TTL vault entry) - k0s vs kubeadm for smaller customer fleets: pros/cons doc needed. - Add automated firmware step: vendor APIs into terraform? (Mateo investigating Dell iDRAC API behavior). - Add simple post-install acceptance test that validates tail-latency SLO for API within 500ms from pivot node. Quick references and links (internal): - Infra provisioner repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-provisioner/pull/412 - Customer handoff template: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/OPS/Onprem+Handoff+Checklist - Jira for rollout automation: JIRA-ENG-4762 Notes to self (choppy): - remove full kubeconfig from terraform outputs (we did once, whoops). - add small terraform wrapper that validates node ip reachability before apply. - coordinate with solutions-eng before any on-site demo. Session log snippets (for context): - "spent 90m chasing PXE - turned out to be stale tftp on switch cache" - "vSphere clone task hung at 32% for 15min -> resolved by datastore cleanup" Appendix: quick terraform apply template (local-exec wrapper idea) - ./scripts/terraform-apply-wrapper.sh

# wraps terraform apply with 3 retries, backoff, and blames the provider logs into /tmp/tf-apply-logs End of draft. -- Priya Nambiar (eng-private-deployments)
